warnings: This is primarily an OZONE study with CO2 as a secondary factor - the core design is ozone × CO2 factorial, not a simple elevated CO2 vs. ambient CO2 comparison

There is NO pure 'elevated CO2 vs. ambient CO2' treatment pair without ozone confounding. The NF+CO2 treatment uses nonfiltered air (5-10% less ozone than ambient), not charcoal-filtered air, so it is not a clean CO2-only comparison vs. ambient
The correct CO2 comparison for meta-analysis purposes is NF+CO2 vs. NF (both at ambient ozone levels), NOT EO+CO2 vs. EO (which includes elevated ozone)
Abstract states '550±50 ppm CO2' but the Methods section states '500±50 ppm CO2' and Table 1 states '500±50 ppm CO2' - there is an inconsistency in reported CO2 target level
The charcoal-filtered (CF) treatment removes 80-85% of ambient ozone AND is at ambient CO2 - this is not a CO2 treatment comparison and should not be used as CO2 control
Two years of data (2009-10 and 2010-11) are reported separately - each year should be treated as a separate observation or averaged carefully
Ozone concentrations differed between years (AOT40: 12.74 vs. 16.96 ppm hour), meaning background conditions differ between years
No variance data is reported in Table 4 (macronutrients/micronutrients) for individual treatment means - only SEM and CD are provided at the bottom pooled across treatments
The 'Ambient control' (AC) treatment is chamber-less ambient air and is very close to NF in all outcomes - NF is the appropriate OTC control
Risk of T/C confusion: multiple treatment groups exist; only NF+CO2 vs. NF is the relevant elevated CO2 comparison for this meta-analysis
recon.variance_source: Standard error of means (SEM) and critical difference (CD) at 5% level of significance were worked out for each parameter.
recon.control_definition: Nonfiltered air (NF): 5-10% less than ambient O3 and ambient CO2 (~385 ppm). This is the OTC control at ambient CO2.
recon.treatment_definition: Nonfiltered air with elevated CO2 (NF+CO2): NF air plus 500±50 ppm CO2. This is the elevated CO2 treatment at ambient ozone levels.
recon.potential_tc_confusion: HIGH RISK: Multiple treatment rows exist in each table. The EO+CO2 treatment also contains elevated CO2 but is confounded with elevated ozone. The CF treatment has sub-ambient ozone which inflates values relative to NF. Extractors must use only NF vs. NF+CO2 comparison for the CO2 effect on mineral concentrations.
recon.sample_size_source: The experiment was carried out with six treatments arranged in completely randomized design with three replications.
recon.factorial_structure: ["CO2 level (ambient vs. elevated)", "ozone level (sub-ambient CF, ambient NF, elevated EO)", "year (2009-10, 2010-11)"]
recon.extraction_guidance: For this meta-analysis, extract mineral concentrations from Table 4 only. The relevant comparison is NF+CO2 (treatment) vs. NF (control) for each mineral (Ca, Mg, S, Zn, Fe) and each year separately. The CO2 level is approximately 500±50 ppm elevated vs. ambient (~385 ppm). Use SEM values provided at the bottom of Table 4 as the variance measure (n=3 replicates). Note that the NF+CO2 vs. NF comparison occurs under ambient ozone conditions (not elevated ozone), making it the cleanest CO2 effect estimate. Do NOT extract EO+CO2 vs. EO as a CO2 comparison for this meta-analysis because ozone confounding makes it unsuitable. Do NOT use CF as the CO2 control. Treat 2009-10 and 2010-11 as separate data points or average them. Protein in Table 3 may also be extracted if the meta-analysis includes N/protein, using the same NF+CO2 vs. NF comparison. The SEM values in Table 4 appear to be pooled across all treatments - use these with caution and note they may underestimate within-treatment variance.
